claim: For every n,m positive lengths s,t>=3, e(Q)>=max((s-2)m1+sum(m),(t-2)n1+sum(n)) for joint residual, and any original Ramsey host satisfies e(G)>=max((s-1)m1+sum(m),(t-1)n1+sum(n)). In particular for red matching n=1^s, exact joint J=(s-2)m1+sum(m), exact original W=(s-1)m1+sum(m), regardless of m profile and parity.
proof: For every vertex set S of size <=length(red_target)-1, red all edges touching S; red graph matching number<=|S| so no red star forest; blue full opposing star forest must lie in G-S. Sequentially choose and delete maximum blue-star centre with degree >=m1 in current residual; count disjoint m1 edges per step, then full surviving forest edges.
context: Strict strengthening of previous saturated matching prefix theorem; no dependence on source-proved Lovasz/core transfer needed for original matching result.
